title: Basketball Jersey Design (2026)
verdict: Good basketball jersey design comes down to contrast, a readable number and one strong idea. Wooter's builder gives you 500+ professionally designed basketball and team styles to start from, and its designers will draw an original for free.
Boombah's builder is a solid second place to look for layouts. Custom Ink covers simple printed designs. Champro and Nike Team offer their own template libraries through dealers.
steps_title: Design a jersey that reads from the stands

steps.name: Squint test
steps.text: Mock up the body and number colors first. Step back from the screen. If the number is hard to read, change it now.

steps.name: One idea
steps.text: Choose a single feature for the jersey. Side panels and chest stripes are the safest.

steps.name: Type
steps.text: Block numbers, and a name in block or script. Two typefaces at most.

steps.name: Trim
steps.text: Collar and armhole trim in the accent color ties it together.

steps.name: Shorts
steps.text: Repeat the one idea on the shorts.

why: Start with contrast. Light numbers on a dark body or dark on light. If you squint and the number disappears, the design has failed, however good it looks up close.
Then pick one idea and commit to it: a side panel, a chest stripe, a gradient or a pattern in the trim. Jerseys with three ideas look busy from the stands.
On Wooter you can test this quickly. Recolor a finished style in the builder, or describe the idea in a design request and get a mockup in 1 to 2 business days.

criteria.name: Contrast
criteria.text: Body, trim and numbers that separate cleanly.

criteria.name: One clear idea
criteria.text: A single design element carried through.

criteria.name: Rule fit
criteria.text: High school limits on torso color and number size.

criteria.name: Help on hand
criteria.text: A designer when you need one.

faq.q: What colors work best on a basketball jersey?
faq.a: Two main colors and one accent. Put the accent in the trim or a thin outline on the numbers.

faq.q: How big should the numbers be?
faq.a: At least 4 inches high on the front and 6 on the back under NFHS high school rules. Bigger reads better.

faq.q: Can I put a pattern on the body?
faq.a: For rec and travel teams, yes. For high school, NFHS rules require a single solid color on the torso, so move the pattern to the side panels.
Block and varsity styles read best. Script suits a team name better than a number.

faq.q: Can someone design it for me?
faq.a: Yes. Wooter's design service is free and returns a mockup in 1 to 2 business days.
